:::{#thm-source-coding}
#### Source coding theorem

Let $X$ be a discrete random variable
that takes finitely many values, at least two of them with positive probability,
and let $\entropyf{X}$ be its
[entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
with base-2 logarithms.

1. Every [uniquely decodable](#def-uniquely-decodable) binary code for $X$
   has [expected length](#def-expected-length) $L \ge \entropyf{X}$.

2. Some uniquely decodable binary code for $X$ has expected length
   $L < \entropyf{X} + 1$.

3. Coding blocks of $n$ independent copies of $X$ at a time,
   some uniquely decodable binary code spends, on average,
   fewer than $\entropyf{X} + 1/n$ [binary digits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) per copy.

:::
